stances.claim: All six points of media concern about Martires were known to and vetted by the JBC -- which, after a lengthy interview on November 16, 2016, found him worthy and nominated him.
stances.rhetorical_move: JBC-vetting trump card against ad hominem attacks

stances.claim: On Item 1, the Duterte canal-cover case was correctly dismissed -- the mayor could not be held liable for demolishing a structure built without permits that caused flooding.
stances.rhetorical_move: factual endorsement of the dismissal on its merits

stances.claim: On Item 3, Martires showed judicial courage in his JBC interview opinions -- specifically dissenting from the Enrile bail grant because advanced age is not among the law's grounds for bail.
San Beda alumni include both Duterte's closest allies and his harshest critics (de Lima, Saguisag) -- alumni connection does not imply subservience.
stances.rhetorical_move: counter-example refutation of the school-loyalty inference

stances.claim: Martires belongs to the Analytical School of Jurisprudence -- he adheres faithfully to the text of laws and firmly stuck to his conviction despite heavy JBC grilling.
The three main judiciary problems Martires identifies -- corruption, government interference, trial by publicity -- are credible and appropriately challenging targets.
stances.rhetorical_move: endorsement of the incoming justice's judicial agenda

notable_anecdotes: Martires and three SBN colleagues going to Davao for an out-of-town hearing and meeting Duterte upon his invitation -- in the meeting, Duterte talked only of his student days, war on drugs, Mindanao history, and respect for the judiciary; no cases mentioned.

Martires's JBC interview opinions: (a) Marcos burial is more political than justiciable; (b) GMA should be acquitted (no ill-gotten wealth proof); (c) Enrile bail was wrongly granted since advanced age is not a statutory ground -- an unusually candid and mixed position.

Pangan v. Ganay (December 4, 2004) -- the SC upheld Martires's refusal to issue an arrest warrant when prosecutors announced they were moving for dismissal to file against another person -- turning an 'admin charge' for alleged ignorance into a SC-endorsed exercise of discretion.
De Lima and Saguisag as San Beda alumni who are among Duterte's harshest critics -- a pointed counter-example to the 'Bedan = Duterte ally' inference.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban profiles Justice Samuel R. Martires, Duterte's first SC appointee -- a career jurist at RTC Agoo, La Union (2000-2006) and the Sandiganbayan (2006-2017) who drew curiosity when media reported six points of concern: his acquittal of then Mayor Duterte, a Davao meeting with the President, controversial JBC interview opinions, an admin charge, a short stint (retiring January 2, 2019), and his San Beda alumni status. The author responds to each. All six were known to and vetted by the JBC, which interviewed Martires lengthily on November 16, 2016, and found him worthy. On the Duterte acquittal: the canal-cover case was correctly dismissed for lack of probable cause -- Duterte could not be held liable for demolishing a structure built without permits. On the Davao meeting: it was an out-of-town hearing; the President invited the group but spoke only of student days, the drug war, and respect for the judiciary. On controversial opinions: Martires said the Marcos burial was more political than justiciable, agreed GMA should be acquitted for lack of ill-gotten wealth proof, but dissented from Enrile's bail (advanced age is not a statutory ground) -- a notably mixed, courageous position. On the admin charge: Pangan v. Ganay (December 4, 2004) shows the SC upheld Martires's refusal to issue an arrest warrant as a proper exercise of discretion. On the short stint: he should work extra hard, consistent with his promise of independence ('the Court should not be influenced by any king or president'). On San Beda: de Lima and Saguisag are both Bedan critics of Duterte. The author classifies Martires as belonging to the Analytical School of Jurisprudence -- faithful to statutory text, courageous under JBC grilling -- and endorses welcoming him, noting his three target problems: corruption, government interference, and trial by publicity.
